platform_errors: Claims CacheService.getUserCache() is keyed automatically per '(script, deployment, signed-in user)' — the API scopes the user cache by script/add-on and effective user, not by deployment; 'deployment' as a distinguishing key element is not a documented CacheService behavior

overbuilt_items: Entire match state (both boards, shot history, turn state) hosted in Apex/Platform Cache instead of client-only LWC state — justified by 'hiding' the computer fleet from devtools, but there is no other human player to hide it from, so this protects nothing
@AuraEnabled GameService controller validating every shot server-side (anti-cheat) for a single-player-vs-computer game with no stakes or opponent to cheat
Platform Cache partition provisioning as a deployable work item
Custom-object fallback schema stubbed for cache-miss scenarios
Full keyboard-alternative input mode (arrow keys + Enter/Space) as a parallel interaction path to click/tap — not requested for a two-person, same-device, same-input-surface game
ARIA labels announcing selection/turn/game-over for screen readers — accessibility scope beyond what the request asked for

platform_errors: D1 free-tier quota cited as '25M rows read/day, 50k rows written/day' — published Cloudflare free-tier limits are closer to 5M rows read/day and 100k rows written/day (25B reads / 50M writes are Paid-plan monthly figures)

Claims a hand-built Worker Response with a `Cache-Control` header is automatically edge-cached by Cloudflare; dynamically constructed fetch-handler responses are not cached at the edge without explicit Cache API use (`caches.default.put`) or a matching Cache Rule.

Domain-only access arguably narrows 'everyone who plays' to internal domain members without flagging that tradeoff as an open choice
"My games" dashboard listing all active/finished games — a feature beyond the request's two-colleague-per-game scope, not needed since email notifications already carry a direct link
D1 finished-game history/results storage beyond the live match (not requested)
Per-user rate limiting on fire_shot/reconnect (abuse throttling) added beyond the request

platform_errors: Declarative Salesforce 'sharing rules' are criteria/role/group-based and cannot grant access to just the two specific participants of one particular record — that per-record, per-pair visibility requires Apex managed (manual) sharing, not a sharing rule.

Claims HTML Service's sandboxed iframe itself lacks WebSocket/SSE support; the real constraint is that Apps Script's server side has no persistent process to push through, not that the iframe blocks outbound WebSocket connections

Cites 'URL-fetch quotas' as a relevant limit for the polling/RPC traffic, but google.script.run web-app calls aren't governed by the UrlFetchApp quota (which applies to outbound HTTP calls the script itself makes); the actually relevant limits are execution time/simultaneous-execution quotas and Sheets read/write limits.

Claims Salesforce's 'built-in optimistic concurrency (via LastModifiedDate)' automatically resolves simultaneous writes for custom Apex DML/LWC saves — that stale-object check only applies to the standard Salesforce UI edit/save flow, not to custom Apex controller updates unless explicitly coded.

Claims polling traffic is 'trivial against org daily API limits' — @AuraEnabled Apex methods invoked from LWC via @wire/imperative calls do not consume the org's daily REST/SOAP API request quota; that limit governs external API integrations, not internal Lightning UI calls.

overbuilt_items: CDC + empApi persistent push subscription (with replay-ID and reconnect handling) chosen for a 1-minute freshness bar, where a simple polling refresh would fit the quota and avoid subscribe/unsubscribe lifecycle complexity

platform_errors: LockService has no automatic '~30s default wait' — a timeout must be explicitly passed to tryLock()/waitLock().

overbuilt_items: Custom Sheets+LockService approval state machine built from scratch instead of considering Google Workspace's native approval/workflow automation features

platform_errors: Claims HtmlService 'doesn't support' polling — polling is achievable via client-side google.script.run calls on an interval; only persistent server-pushed WebSocket connections are unsupported.

Claims 'native role-hierarchy inheritance' would grant managers access to reports' records if Manager__c is backed by User.ManagerId — Salesforce's native 'grant access using hierarchies' follows Role hierarchy, not the User.ManagerId field; sharing by manager relationship requires an explicit sharing rule or Apex-managed sharing, not automatic inheritance.

States a flat '6-minute execution ceiling' for Apps Script, but the domain-restricted deployment implies a Google Workspace account, where the script runtime limit is 30 minutes, not 6 — the plan's own quota check is inconsistent with its deployment target.

overbuilt_items: Client-side 5-minute auto-refresh polling timer while the dashboard tab is open — the request only requires data to be no more than 15 minutes stale on view, not continuous background polling; a plain load-time fetch against the 900s cache already satisfies this.

5-minute client-side setInterval auto-polling layered on top of an already-live per-load aggregate query — the request only needs figures no more than 15 minutes stale, which a simple query-on-visit already satisfies without a standing refresh timer

Authenticated GET /orders?date= endpoint (work item 7) — request only asks that reports can use the stored data; direct D1 binding from an in-account reports Worker suffices without adding an auth-protected HTTP surface
Authenticated backfill HTTP endpoint with shared-secret/Access auth — adds a request-driven access surface and credential-check feature the nightly batch request never asked for
platform_errors: Claim that 'Cloudflare won't overlap two invocations of the same cron schedule, so no cross-run locking is needed' is not a documented Cron Trigger guarantee — Cloudflare's own retry behavior on scheduled-handler failure is precisely why the plan needs idempotent upserts elsewhere, which contradicts treating overlap as impossible

Cloudflare D1 free tier is stated as '25M reads/day' — the actual free-tier limit is approximately 5 million rows read/day (25 billion rows read/month is a Workers Paid-plan monthly included allotment, not a free-tier daily figure).
'LockService.getScriptLock() waits ≤30s by default' is inaccurate — the lock has no default wait; a timeout must be explicitly passed to waitLock(timeoutInMillis).

overbuilt_items: Optional reCAPTCHA v3 UrlFetchApp integration (work item 10) adds scope beyond the honeypot/timing/rate-limit controls that already satisfy the 'protected from spam' requirement
platform_errors: Session.getActiveUser().getEmail() is unlikely to reliably identify staff when the web app is deployed with Access: Anyone — Apps Script generally only exposes active-user identity when the deployment requires sign-in (e.g., restricted to a domain or 'Anyone with Google account'); under a fully open 'Anyone' deployment it commonly returns a blank string even for logged-in staff, so the described domain-gate check may fail to identify legitimate staff and cannot be trusted as the sole authorization mechanism

overbuilt_items: reopenSubmission + resolver notes go slightly beyond the requested 'read and resolve' workflow

platform_errors: Describes Advanced Drive Service calls as going 'via UrlFetchApp' — Advanced Services are invoked through their generated wrapper methods (e.g. Drive.Files.insert) with OAuth handled internally, not via the developer calling UrlFetchApp directly.

overbuilt_items: Bound-Sheet audit log of every receipt (email, timestamp, Drive link, total, date) is added as a 'default' beyond the literal 'show the result' ask, without an explicit deletion/expiry policy
Admin permission set with org-wide 'View All' visibility for Receipt__c — an admin/reviewer role was not requested; the scenario only asks for the uploading employee to see their own result

Platform Events + empApi/CometD live-push subscription to deliver a single-user async OCR result, when the request only needs the employee to see the result on next visit or via notification (expected tier explicitly excludes a live channel)
Platform Event + empApi/CometD live subscription channel for completion notice, exceeding the tier's 'no live channel' scope (next-visit re-query or a platform/email notification would suffice)
platform_errors: Claim that Change Data Capture (CDC) requires an edition/Shield entitlement is inaccurate — CDC availability is edition-gated (Enterprise/Unlimited/Performance/Developer), and Salesforce Shield (Platform Encryption/Event Monitoring/Field Audit Trail) is an unrelated add-on with no bearing on CDC access

overbuilt_items: Author-only edit/delete permission modeling and negative-test coverage for a delete/edit capability the request never asked for (only post/view/scroll)
platform_errors: Claims a permission set can grant 'no Edit/Delete except author-owner' on Chat_Message__c — Salesforce permission-set/profile CRUD is all-or-nothing per object, not conditional on a custom Author__c lookup; per-record owner restriction needs the record's real OwnerId with sharing rules or explicit Apex/trigger enforcement, which the plan never specifies

Asserts empApi 'handles reconnection internally' as sufficient for resync, but CometD auto-reconnect does not guarantee delivery of events missed during the disconnect window without explicit replay/replayId handling, which the plan does not configure

Claims Mobile Offline for LWC "GA since Summer '23, supported at API 62.0" — Summer '23 corresponds to API v58.0, not v62.0 (which is Winter '25); the release-season/API-version pairing is internally inconsistent.

Claims Salesforce Mobile App LWC offline support (offline pages, local draft cache, automatic sync via Lightning Data Service) has existed 'since Spring '23' — this Mobile Offline/LWC offline capability rolled out later (Summer '23 beta and subsequent GA), not Spring '23.

Claims the Apps Script per-execution runtime cap is 6 minutes for Google Workspace accounts; Workspace accounts actually get a 30-minute execution cap, and 6 minutes is the consumer (gmail.com) account limit.

The plan claims a 'fetch-level timeout budget' can be applied to UrlFetchApp via muteHttpExceptions; muteHttpExceptions only suppresses exceptions on non-2xx HTTP responses and has no relation to timeouts — Apps Script's UrlFetchApp does not expose a configurable timeout parameter at all.
